summary: Kootenai National Forest lookout rebuilt in 2011 after earlier 1932 and 1960s-era towers; now a car-accessible rental.

access.note: Car accessible; rented through Recreation.gov, late June through mid-October.

visit.trail_note: Mountain roads lead directly to the lookout; access depends on weather.

events.note: First lookout: a 10-foot pole tower with L-4 cab.
NHLR dates a replacement tower to 1968; firelookout.com instead describes a treated-timber tower from the 1950s, so the exact year is disputed.
Last year the lookout is recorded as staffed.
Present 5-foot tower with replica L-4 cab built, entering the recreation rental program.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 3, 2014.

evidence.supports: Named for Col. David Minton, buried near Minton Creek
evidence.quote: The mountain was named after Col. David Minton, Ohio cavalryman who homesteaded (and is buried) near the mouth of Minton Creek.

evidence.supports: First lookout 1932, pole tower L-4 cab
evidence.quote: The first tower was a 10' pole tower with L-4 cab built in 1932.

A 10' treated timber tower with L-4 cab was set up in the 1950s. It was last staffed in 1973. A new replica L-4 cab on a new 5' tower, constructed in 2011, was added to the Recreation Rental program. Known lookout personnel: 1967: Helen Ahlgren.

evidence.supports: Elevation 5,351 ft, car accessible, late June-mid October season, no water, sleeps guests, pack out trash
evidence.quote: Minton Peak Lookout is situated in the Rocky Mountains at an elevation of 5,351 feet in the Kootenai National Forest... The lookout is typically open from late June through mid-October and is accessible by car.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states the replacement tower (between the 1932 structure and the 2011 rebuild) dates to 1968, while firelookout.com describes a treated-timber tower erected in the 1950s. Both may refer to the same structure under different dating; kept both and flagged in the story.

notes_for_editor: Middle-tower date conflict (1950s vs 1968) not resolvable from available sources; flagged in story and resolved_conflicts. No NRHP nomination found for this tower. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the 'named for Col. David Minton' and 'first tower, 1932' sentences were mis-cited to source 1 (NHLR); that page does not contain either sentence verbatim (it instead says the original pole tower 'was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1932'). Both sentences are verbatim on source 2 (firelookout.com), and the Minton-name sentence is also verbatim on source 3 (Recreation.gov); citations corrected and the unsupported 'by the early 2000s the old tower was gone' claim was removed from the story.
